title: Add support for NetBird VPN (org.freedesktop.NetworkManager.netbird) in plasma-nm
line: NetBird VPN connections can now be created, edited and connected from Plasma's network settings and Networks widget.
explanation: plasma-nm only activates VPN connections whose type has a Plasma VPN plugin, and there was none for NetBird, so clicking Connect on a NetBird profile made with nmcli only showed "Plasma is missing support for 'netbird' VPN connections". The connection editor also had no VPN tab for it and NetBird was not offered as a new connection type. The change adds a vpn/netbird plugin like the existing ones: an editor for the NetBird data keys (auth mode, setup key, management/admin URL, username, hostname, interface name, pre-shared key) and a secrets prompt that answers the NetBird service's setup-key and SSO requests (login link and code, then continue).

commits.message:
vpn: add NetBird plugin

NetBird connections made with nmcli could not be connected from Plasma,
which refuses VPN types it has no plugin for. This adds an editor for
the NetBird settings and a prompt for its setup key and SSO login.

BUG: 527352

media.caption: Master: Connect on a NetBird profile only shows "Plasma is missing support for 'netbird' VPN connections"
Fix: Connect goes through to NetworkManager; when NetBird asks for SSO, Plasma shows the login page and code
Master: no NetBird in the list of new VPN connection types
Fix: NetBird is offered as a new VPN connection type
Master: the NetBird profile has no VPN settings tab
Fix: the VPN (netbird) tab with the NetBird settings, setup-key mode selected

review.text: Adds a vpn/netbird plugin modelled closely on the existing VPN plugins (editor widget, secrets prompt, JSON with X-NetworkManager-Services), which is exactly how plasma-nm supports a new NM VPN type, and it has no effect on other VPN types. Verification is against a dbusmock NetworkManager and the hint/key names from NetBird's NM plugin docs, not a real NetBird daemon, so the SSO/setup-key exchange should be confirmed with a real NetBird setup (or by a NetBird user on the MR) before merging.
